solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Artistic Italian in Group E, oddly

indicators.note: done oddly, the letters of these words are arranged in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A World Cup draw note: an arty Italian player turns up in Group E.
explanation.walkthrough: PERUGINO was an Italian Renaissance painter, teacher of Raphael.
explanation.definitionFit: Pietro Perugino was a Renaissance painter from Umbria, so he is an artist from Italy.

clue.text: Wings of 7 and 25 affected by nerves

indicators.note: the wings of a team are its two flanks, so we take the first and last letters of each answer named

parts.note: 7-across is ENGLAND
25-across is GERMANY

explanation.surface: The wide players of England and Germany are jittery before their big match.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy is an everyday adjective for tense, anxious or on edge.

clue.text: Leading players thrown in the air

parts.note: a side that is leading is up, ahead in the score
the players in a show are its cast

explanation.surface: Star players are hoisted aloft by celebrating fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Upcast is an old adjective for something tossed or directed upwards.

clue.text: Final outcome expected this evening — and news story frantically absorbing one?

indicators.note: absorbing means soaking something up, so the letter is taken inside the jumble
done frantically, these letters are thrown into wild disorder

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Sports reporters scramble over the outcome of tonight's final.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle AND plus NEWS STORY and absorb I (one) to get TODAY'S WINNERS, the answer split over 4 and 19 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever takes tonight's final will be the champions of the day, the result awaited that evening.

clue.text: Make grade, somehow, after he secures a cap, say

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following HE

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: secures means holds fast, so the jumbled letters hold the A within them
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A player earns his international cap after making the grade.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests HE holds the A, but it is the shuffled letters that take it in; 'Make' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap is one example of headwear; 'say' marks it as an instance of the broader category.

clue.text: Run into supporter before church in country

indicators.note: before places the first part ahead of the church abbreviation
into puts the run abbreviation inside the word for a supporter

parts.note: a supporter of a team is a fan
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A fan runs into a supporter on the way to church somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a nation in western Europe and a World Cup side.

clue.text: Team not great, to begin with, in game in South Africa

indicators.note: in places the opening letters inside the antelope

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope, game animal of the veld

indicators.note: to begin with points to the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A lacklustre England side play a match at the South Africa World Cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like a football match, but it is the hunted animal: the eland.
explanation.definitionFit: England are a national football side, one of the competing squads.

clue.text: Beastly noise from team-leader after end of morning jog

indicators.note: after puts the team leader's letter following the others
end of picks the final letter of morning

parts.note: to jog is to run slowly
the leading letter of team

explanation.surface: The skipper gasps loudly after an early-morning training run.
explanation.definitionFit: A grunt is the low guttural sound made by a pig or similar animal.

clue.text: A stern chat that is followed by unfair penalty for Americans?

parts.note: the stern is the rear, and bum is slang for the backside
rap is slang for chat or talk

explanation.surface: A harsh telling-off, then a referee's dodgy penalty in a US match.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang a bum rap is a false charge or undeserved punishment.

clue.text: United embraced by supporter, innovative type

indicators.note: embraced by means held within, so the word for united goes inside the support

parts.note: a pier is a pillar that supports a bridge
united means made one

explanation.surface: A Manchester United player is hugged by a fan, an inventive sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' and 'supporter' suggest football; here they are ONE and a bridge PIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is someone who leads the way in new ideas or methods, a trailblazer.

clue.text: Year a university teacher backed champions twice

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: a guru is a spiritual teacher

explanation.surface: Every year a university lecturer bets on the double champions.
explanation.definitionFit: Uruguay won football's World Cup in 1930 and again in 1950, two titles.

clue.text: A group of players picked for lack of inhibition

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians playing together
a player picked for the team is on it

explanation.surface: A squad has been selected for its carefree attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: To act with abandon is to behave freely, without restraint.

clue.text: Dramatically play in Italian team ready for French

parts.note: Inter Milan, the Italian football club, is called Inter
French for ready is pret

explanation.surface: An Italian side performing theatrically, all set to face France.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor interprets a role, bringing out its meaning on stage.

clue.text: Man on pitch not playing part of centre-forward

indicators.note: part of means only some of the letters, so the answer lies inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A striker is benched and sits out the match.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an injured striker; the hint is the official on the field who never plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The referee is on the field throughout the match but takes no part as a player.

clue.text: Piece of play witnessed by spectators, say

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the word, so it is matched by sound

parts.note: what spectators witness is seen

explanation.surface: A passage of play watched by the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a division of a stage drama, one section of the action.

clue.text: Elated, like 4 19 and their predecessors herein

definitions.meaning: first meaning: overjoyed, in high spirits
second meaning: the winners of the final and past champions in this grid rank highest on the globe

explanation.walkthrough: The grid holds past World Cup winners; with the new winners, they are literally the best in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes extreme happiness, and world champions sit above every other nation.

clue.text: Get to instant replay, initially — argument follows next day

indicators.note: follows puts the quarrel word after the other pieces

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of replay

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: The pundits get to the instant replay, then a row breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomorrow is the day after today.

clue.text: Swine ending off match with own goal

indicators.note: ending off picks the last letter of the word

parts.note: OG is the football abbreviation for own goal

explanation.surface: A rotten player settles the game by scoring into his own net.
explanation.definitionFit: A hog is a pig, and swine is the general word for pigs.

clue.text: See 4
Dreadfully saddened in positions in which goals are blocked

definitions.text: positions in which goals are blocked

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests things in a terrible mess, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Fans are crushed by a game where every attack is stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goals' are aims in life, not football goals.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead end is a situation offering no way forward, where progress towards an aim is impossible.

clue.text: Stop fighting in extremely disruptive and unruly crowd

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: a mob is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A very disruptive, lawless mob of fans is told to stop brawling.
explanation.definitionFit: To demob is to discharge troops from military service when war ends, so they leave combat.

clue.text: Place for coaches and subs removed from ground

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sheltered bench by the pitch for managers and substitutes
second meaning: excavated, taken out of the earth

explanation.walkthrough: 'coaches' could be buses and 'ground' a stadium; both senses are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: The trackside shelter is a hollowed-out bench, and as a past participle the phrase means excavated soil.

clue.text: Supporter upset girl, a kind of nut

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Liz is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A fan upsets a girl who is a bit of a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brazil nut is the large seed of a South American tree.

clue.text: Aren't in a combination that includes good SA side

indicators.note: the three words run together as one combination, which then takes the extra letter inside it

explanation.surface: A South American side who aren't in a winning combination.
explanation.walkthrough: SA here means South America, not South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a South American nation whose football team are double world champions.

clue.text: Stupidly annoy European who might win evenly balanced game?

definitions.text: who might win evenly balanced game?

indicators.note: done stupidly, these letters are put in a foolish order

explanation.surface: A daft European irritating everyone over an evenly matched game.
explanation.definitionFit: When a game is wide open, anybody at all could be its winner.

clue.text: One score one left out for this team

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: out means missing, so a letter is removed from the scorecount

parts.note: a tally is a running score
L is the abbreviation for left, and only one of the two goes

explanation.surface: A team is one goal down and a player is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a national football side, four times world champions.

clue.text: Rival team that could make me angry

indicators.note: could make says the letters might be rearranged to form a new word

explanation.surface: An England fan admits the old enemy side really annoys them.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany are England's traditional football opponents, the classic adversary.

clue.text: Cheat badly with first couple of penalties in part of SA

indicators.note: badly means done wrongly, so the letters are mixed up
first couple of takes the opening two letters of penalties

explanation.surface: A player cheats badly to win the first two penalties in a South African match.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cape is the southwestern region of South Africa, around Cape Town.

clue.text: Control football, getting some upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: some means a part of something

explanation.surface: A player controls the ball while some of the fans get upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap the ball in football is to stop it dead and bring it under control.

clue.text: You said a point, potentially, is the best one can get

indicators.note: said tells us the word is spoken, giving a single letter with the same sound

parts.note: the letter U sounds like you

indicators.note: potentially means possibly, so these letters may become another word

explanation.surface: A pundit insists one point could be the best result available.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian describes an ideal, perfect state of affairs, the most that could be hoped for.

clue.text: Evaluated and backed South Africa, for example, with editor

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: say means for example

explanation.surface: An editor assessed the odds and bet on South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay is to test or analyse something, typically a metal, to judge its quality.
